title: Halving the source register
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $o$ be an oracle on five deciders and bit strings, and let $y$ be a bit string. For any fifteen-register state $st$ whose register values are all at most $B$, the program reaches a configuration from the initial one with label the halving routine in phase $0$, register values $st$, and no result, whose label is the copy routine transferring the source register to the scratch register, whose loop counter is $0$, whose source register is the original source value divided by $2$ raised to the original loop-counter value, and whose other registers agree with $st$. Every configuration strictly before the reached configuration satisfies the guard requiring all registers to be at most $B$ and the instruction-specific preconditions to hold.
hypotheses_covered: $o$ is an oracle on five deciders and bit strings
$st$ has all fifteen registers at most $B$
replaced:
Fix natural numbers $a,b,f,B$, a Boolean mode, an oracle assigning a Boolean answer to
each of five deciders and each bit string, and an input bit string. For every register
state whose fifteen register values are all at most $B$, the program started at its
halving routine in phase $0$ reaches the copy routine that transfers the source register
to the scratch register, with the loop counter reset to $0$ and the source register
replaced by its original value divided by $2$ to the power of its original loop-counter
value. Every configuration before the reached configuration satisfies the program's
guard requiring all registers to remain at most $B$ and all instruction-specific
preconditions to hold.
